newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ sets Dec long-term prime at record low 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: IBJ sets Dec long-term prime at record low 2.5 pct.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ) said on Monday it would cut its long-term prime rate by 0.2 percentage point to a record low 2.5 percent for December, effective from Wednesday.
IBJ said it would set the coupon rate of its debenture to be issued this month at 1.6 percent, down from 1.8 percent in November.
The bank customarily sets its long-term prime rate, that at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, 0.9 percentage point above its debenture coupon rate.
The previous record low for the long-term prime rate was 2.6 percent in December 1995.
IBJ revises the rates every month to reflect market trends.
